translations.idiomatic: When Shouzheng died, the Emperor learned that his family was destitute and ordered a monthly stipend of ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 守素，咸平中為侍禁，亦貧，真宗賜白金百兩，語宰相曰：「諸偽主子孫率多窘迫，蓋僭侈之後不知稼穡艱難所致也。」

translations.literal: Shousu, in the Xianping era, served as Palace Attendant and was also poor; Zhenzong bestowed one hundred taels of white gold and told the chief ministers: "The sons and grandsons of the various false lords are mostly in straitened circumstances — after lives of extravagant usurpation they do not know the hardship of farming."
translations.idiomatic: Shousu served as a Palace Attendant during the Xianping era and was likewise impoverished. Zhenzong granted him one hundred taels of silver and told the chief ministers, "The descendants of the former usurping rulers are mostly in want — bred to extravagance, they never learned the labor that fills the granary."

sentences.zh: 後至內殿崇班，天禧中，又錄為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Later he reached the Inner Hall Honored Class; in the Tianxi era he was again enrolled as Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to the Inner Hall Honored Class, and in the Tianxi era was appointed Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 守通，供奉官。

translations.literal: Shoutong was a Tribute Official.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutong served as a Tribute Official.

sentences.zh: 守正子克昌，為三班奉職；

translations.literal: Shouzheng's son Kechang was a Third-Rank Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzheng's son Kechang held the rank of Third-Rank Attendant;

sentences.zh: 國昌，為借職。

translations.literal: Guochang was granted a borrowed (acting) office.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang held only a provisional acting commission.

sentences.zh: 龔澄樞，廣州南海人。

translations.literal: Gong Chengshu was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Chengshu came from Nanhai in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性廉謹，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: His character was honest and careful; he did not socialize casually.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and cautious by nature and kept few companions.

sentences.zh: 幼事龑為內供奉官，累遷內給事。

translations.literal: In youth he served the emperor with the invented name as Inner Tribute Official and was repeatedly promoted to Inner Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he entered service under the emperor with the invented name as an Inner Tribute Official and rose through successive posts to Inner Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 晟襲位，任閹人林延遇為甘泉宮使，頗預政事。

translations.literal: When Shen succeeded to the throne, he appointed the eunuch Lin Yanyu Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, and Yanyu took considerable part in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen took the throne, he made the eunuch Lin Yanyu Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, and Lin came to wield considerable influence over state affairs.

sentences.zh: 延遇病將死，言於晟曰：「臣死，惟龔澄樞可用。」

translations.literal: Yanyu, ill and near death, said to Shen: "When I die, only Gong Chengshu can be used."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Yanyu told Shen, "When I am gone, only Gong Chengshu is fit to serve you."

sentences.zh: 即日擢知承宣院兼內侍省，改德陵使兼龍德宮使。

translations.literal: That same day he was promoted to administer the Presentation Court while also holding the Palace Domestic Service, then transferred to Commissioner of the Virtue Mausoleum together with Commissioner of the Dragon Virtue Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Shen promoted him to head the Presentation Court while also serving in the Palace Domestic Service, then made him Commissioner of the Virtue Mausoleum and Commissioner of the Dragon Virtue Palace.

sentences.zh: 鋹嗣位，加特進、開府儀同三司、萬華宮使、驃騎大將軍，改上將軍、左龍虎軍觀軍容使、內太師，軍國之務皆決於澄樞。

translations.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu was given Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General; he was then changed to Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor — all military and state affairs were decided by Chengshu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General, then Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor. Every matter of war and state passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 澄樞與李托、薛崇譽置酷法之具，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Chengshu, together with Li Tuo and Xue Chongyu, set up instruments of cruel law, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshu, Li Tuo, and Xue Chongyu instituted instruments of torture, and the people endured terrible suffering.

sentences.zh: 初，岩改名龔，有術者言不利，名龔，當敗國事，遂改名龑。

translations.literal: At first Yan changed his name to Gong; a diviner said it was unfavorable — the name Gong would ruin state affairs — so he changed his name to the invented character.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had first changed his name to Gong, but a diviner warned that the name Gong would bring ruin upon the state, so he adopted the invented character instead.

sentences.zh: 後鋹用澄樞，以其姓卒亡其國，澄樞亦被誅。

translations.literal: Later Chang employed Chengshu; because of his surname he ultimately lost his state, and Chengshu was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chang put Chengshu in power — and the Gong surname did indeed destroy his realm. Chengshu was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 李托，封州封川人。

translations.literal: Li Tuo was a native of Fengchuan in Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tuo came from Fengchuan in Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少習騎射，以謹願事龑為內府局令。

translations.literal: In youth he practiced mounted archery and, with cautious compliance, served the emperor with the invented name as Director of an Inner Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in horsemanship and archery from youth and entered service under the emperor with the invented name as Director of an Inner Treasury Bureau, distinguished by his dutiful temperament.

sentences.zh: 晟襲位，遷內侍省內侍，充宮闈諸衛押番兼秀華宮使。

translations.literal: When Shen succeeded to the throne, Tuo was transferred to Palace Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, filling the palace guard rotation duty together with Commissioner of the Splendid Beauty Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen took the throne, Tuo was made a Palace Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, assigned to the palace guard rotation and Commissioner of the Splendid Beauty Palace.

sentences.zh: 鋹立，改玩華宮使、內侍監兼列聖、景陽二宮使。

translations.literal: When Chang established himself on the throne, Tuo was changed to Commissioner of the Playful Splendor Palace and Superintendent of the Palace Domestic Service, together with Commissioner of the Two Ancestor Palaces of Liesheng and Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took the throne, Tuo became Commissioner of the Playful Splendor Palace and Superintendent of the Palace Domestic Service, while also overseeing the Liesheng and Jingyang ancestral palaces.

sentences.zh: 托納二女於鋹，鋹以其長為貴妃，次為美人，政事皆訪托而後行。

translations.literal: Tuo presented two daughters to Chang; Chang made the elder Honored Consort and the younger a Beauty, and all government affairs were consulted with Tuo before being carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo gave two daughters to Chang in marriage; the elder became Honored Consort and the younger a Beauty. No policy moved forward until Tuo had been consulted.

sentences.zh: 加特進、開府儀同三司、甘泉宮使兼六軍觀軍容使、行內中尉，遷驃騎上將軍、內太師。

translations.literal: He was given the special advancement of Grand Mentor, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace together with Army Observer of the Six Armies, and Acting Inner Captain; he was then promoted to Cavalry Grand General and Inner Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, Army Observer of the Six Armies, and Acting Inner Captain, then rose to Cavalry Grand General and Inner Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太祖命師伐鋹，既克韶州，統軍使李承渥戰死，節度副使辛延渥間道遣人勸鋹降，托堅沮其議。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered an army to attack Chang; after Shao Prefecture was taken, army commander Li Chenwo died in battle, and deputy commissioner Xin Yanwo sent a man by a hidden route to urge Chang to surrender — Tuo firmly blocked the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu sent his army against Chang and Shao Prefecture fell, army commander Li Chenwo was killed in battle. Deputy commissioner Xin Yanwo sent an envoy by a secret route to urge surrender, but Tuo firmly blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及就擒至許田，太祖遣使問托等：「昨已約降，復率眾來拒戰，及軍敗又縱火焚府庫，誰為之謀也？」

translations.literal: When they were captured and brought to Xutian, Taizu dispatched an envoy to question Tuo and the others: "Yesterday you had agreed to surrender, yet again led the masses to resist in battle; when the army was defeated you again set fire and burned the storehouses — who devised this?"
translations.idiomatic: After their capture and arrival at Xutian, Taizu sent an envoy to question Tuo and his associates: "You had already agreed to surrender, yet you rallied troops to fight again, and when defeated you set fire to the storehouses. Who planned this?"

sentences.zh: 托俯首不能對。

translations.literal: Tuo bowed his head and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo hung his head and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 鋹諫議大夫王珪謂托曰：「昔在廣州，機務並爾輩所專，火又自內起，今天子遣使案問，爾復欲推過何人？」

translations.literal: Chang's Remonstrating Censor Wang Gui said to Tuo: "Formerly in Guangzhou, state affairs were all monopolized by you lot; the fire also started from within. Today the Son of Heaven has sent an envoy to investigate — to whom do you again wish to shift the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang's Remonstrating Censor Wang Gui said to Tuo, "In Guangzhou you and your faction controlled every decision; the fire was lit from within the palace. Now the Son of Heaven sends an envoy to investigate — who else do you mean to blame?"

sentences.zh: 遂唾而批其頰，托乃引伏，後至京斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he spat and struck his cheek; Tuo then confessed, and later, upon reaching the capital, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He spat in Tuo's face and struck his cheek. Tuo confessed on the spot and was later executed when they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 薛崇譽，韶州曲江人。

translations.literal: Xue Chongyu was a native of Qujiang in Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Chongyu came from Qujiang in Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善《孫子五曹算》。

translations.literal: He was skilled in Sunzi's Five Methods of Calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in Sunzi's Five Methods of Calculation.

sentences.zh: 晟署為內門使兼太倉使。

translations.literal: Shen appointed him Inner Gate Commissioner together with Grand Granary Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shen appointed him Inner Gate Commissioner and Grand Granary Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鋹嗣位，遷內中尉、特進、開府儀同三司、簽書點檢司事。

translations.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chongyu was promoted to Inner Captain, given special advancement as Grand Mentor and Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and made Secretary of Inspection Bureau Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took the throne, Chongyu became Inner Captain, received Special Advancement and Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and was appointed Secretary of Inspection Bureau Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖命師克廣州，崇譽縱火焚倉廩，擒至京，與李托同戮。

translations.literal: When Taizu ordered the army to capture Guangzhou, Chongyu set fire and burned the granaries; captured and brought to the capital, he was executed together with Li Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu's army took Guangzhou, Chongyu set fire to the granaries. Captured and brought to the capital, he was executed alongside Li Tuo.

sentences.zh: 潘崇徹，廣州南海人。

translations.literal: Pan Chongche was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chongche came from Nanhai in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 事龑為內侍省局丞。

translations.literal: He served the emperor with the invented name as Bureau Assistant in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under the emperor with the invented name as a Bureau Assistant in the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 頗讀兵書，立戰功。

translations.literal: He read military books extensively and established battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He studied military texts and won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 晟嘗遣大將吳懷恩伐桂州平之，懷恩為部下所殺，命崇徹代之。

translations.literal: Shen once dispatched the great general Wu Huai'en to attack Gui Prefecture and pacify it; Huai'en was killed by his subordinates, and Shen ordered Chongche to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen once sent the general Wu Huai'en to conquer Gui Prefecture. When Wu was killed by his own men, Shen put Chongche in command.

sentences.zh: 鋹襲位，加西北面都統。

translations.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chongche was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of the Northwest Area.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took the throne, Chongche was made Commander-in-Chief of the Northwest Area.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，鋹頗疑崇徹，遣薛宗譽使其軍以察之。

translations.literal: After more than a year Chang grew quite suspicious of Chongche and dispatched Xue Chongyu to his army to inspect him.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Chang grew suspicious of Chongche and sent Xue Chongyu to his camp to investigate.

sentences.zh: 崇譽還，遂白崇徹日以伶人百餘衣錦繡、吹玉笛，為長夜之飲，不恤軍政。

translations.literal: Chongyu returned and reported that Chongche daily had more than a hundred actors clad in brocade, blowing jade flutes, holding all-night drinking revels, and not caring for military government.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Chongyu reported that Chongche spent his days with more than a hundred performers in brocade robes, playing jade flutes and feasting through the night while neglecting military affairs.

sentences.zh: 鋹怒，召歸，奪其兵柄，自是居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Chang was angry, summoned him back, and stripped him of military authority; from then on he lived in constant discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Chang recalled him and stripped him of command. Thereafter Chongche lived in perpetual resentment.

sentences.zh: 太祖命師度嶺，鋹復命崇徹領兵五萬戍賀江，崇徹不為效命。

translations.literal: When Taizu ordered the army to cross the mountains, Chang again ordered Chongche to lead fifty thousand troops to garrison the He River; Chongche did not exert himself in service.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu's army crossed the mountains, Chang again put Chongche in charge of fifty thousand troops to guard the He River, but Chongche refused to fight with any zeal.

sentences.zh: 鋹敗，至京，太祖知其事，特赦之，授汝州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: When Chang was defeated and reached the capital, Taizu knew the circumstances, specially pardoned him, appointed him Vice-Governor of Ru Prefecture, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang's defeat Chongche was brought to the capital. Taizu, knowing what had transpired, granted him a special pardon and appointed him Vice-Governor of Ru Prefecture, where he later died.
